query: Sas::Ptp10D interactions also control the elimination of neoplastic epithelial clones by surrounding normal tissue. Sas is on normal epithelial cells, and it relocalizes to the parts of their cell surfaces that are adjacent to the neoplastic clone and binds to Ptp10D on the neoplastic cells. Ptp10D in turn relocalizes and dephosphorylates the EGF receptor tyrosine kinase, leading to death of the neoplastic cells (Yamamoto et al., 2017).
